welcome.title: Welcome to Argus
welcome.body: Argus is a modern task manager for Windows. It shows processes, performance, services, startup apps and network connections, and keeps a history of resource usage. The next few steps set up the essentials. Every step can be skipped, and everything can be changed later in Settings.

display.title: Display and refresh
display.body: Choose the navigation position, animations and refresh rate.
display.navHint: The side pane shows only icons by default and expands to show page names.
display.motionHint: Transitions when switching pages and opening menus and dialogs.
display.chartHint: Higher frame rates are smoother but use more resources.
display.intervalHint: Shorter intervals keep data more current but make Argus itself use more resources.

background.title: Stay in the background
background.body: Argus can keep running in the system tray, recording history and applying rules, ready to open whenever it's needed.
background.autostart: Start when signing in to Windows
background.autostartHint: Starts silently in the system tray, without a window.
background.closeToTray: Keep in the system tray when closed
background.closeToTrayHint: When this is off, closing the window exits Argus.
background.minimizedIntervalHint: 5 seconds by default; shorter intervals cost more in the background.
background.trayIntervalHint: History and rules run at this pace while Argus is in the tray.
background.hotkey: Press {hotkey} anytime to show or hide Argus. The shortcut can be changed in Settings.
background.hotkeyOff: The shortcut for showing or hiding Argus is turned off. It can be turned back on in Settings.

update.title: Stay up to date
update.body: Argus gets new versions from GitHub Releases. Installers must pass a signature check, and nothing is installed without confirmation.
update.checkHint: About a minute after start, then once a day.
update.betaHint: Beta also receives pre-releases: new features sooner, but possibly less stable.
update.proxyNotice: GitHub proxies are run by third parties and can see this PC's IP address and the files it downloads. The signature check keeps them from tampering with updates.

privilege.title: Privileged service (optional)
privilege.body: Argus runs as a standard user, so some system processes can't be read, ended or adjusted. The optional privileged service runs in the background as SYSTEM. Once it's installed, Argus can:

features.end: End other users' processes (except critical system processes)
features.tune: Set priority and efficiency mode, also automatically through rules
features.inspect: Find file locks in every process and measure per-process network traffic
features.control: Control Windows services and close network connections
features.sensors: Provide access to kernel sensors (the driver is enabled separately)

privilege.risk: The permission belongs to the current Windows account: any program running under it can use these functions, which amounts to partial administrator rights. Only install it on an account you use yourself.
privilege.later: Installing requires administrator permission. It can also be skipped and installed or uninstalled later in Settings → Permissions.
privilege.replace: The following steps offer kernel sensors and Task Manager replacement.
privilege.manage: See the details, update or reinstall it in Settings → Permissions.
privilege.elevated: Argus is running as administrator, so process management does not need the privileged service. Kernel sensors and Task Manager replacement still require it.

sensors.title: Kernel sensors (optional)
sensors.body: Read the processor's internal sensors for temperature and power data.
sensors.install: Administrator permission is requested when PawnIO needs to be installed or started.
sensors.needsService: Install and start the privileged service first. An existing service that cannot connect can be updated in Settings.
sensors.later: Off by default. Select Next to skip this option and enable it later in Settings → Permissions.
sensors.manage: View readings on the Performance page and turn sensors off in Settings → Permissions. Turning them off does not uninstall the shared driver.

taskManager.title: Replace Task Manager (optional)
taskManager.body: When on, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Task Manager in the taskbar's context menu and the other ways to open Task Manager open Argus.
taskManager.scope: This applies to the whole PC; other accounts still open Windows Task Manager. If Argus can't start, Windows Task Manager opens instead.
taskManager.undo: It can be turned off anytime in Settings → Permissions, and a standalone recovery tool works even when the interface or the service can't run.
taskManager.later: Turning it on requires administrator permission. It can also be skipped and turned on later in Settings → Permissions.
taskManager.needsService: The replacement relies on the privileged service; install and start it in the Privileged service step first.

tips.title: You're all set
tips.body: A few ways to get around faster:
tips.menu: Right-click a process to end it, change its priority, turn on efficiency mode or add a rule
tips.drop: Drop a file or folder onto the window to find the processes using it
tips.history: The History page keeps the last 7 days of resource usage and the busiest processes at each moment
tips.reopen: This guide can be reopened anytime from Settings → About.
